answer: Because the canyon stake is held until the mirror settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the juniper audit lists each exposure. A farm running 109 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. An attester must stake 11% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
